companionIntegration: Python request transport already goes through functions/lib/nst_admission.py (transferred). Whole Python jobs do not thereby acquire a lifecycle. Enclosing job-level begin/finish/hold would require the exact Python entrypoints listed here, and their tests, if they participate in occupancy.

functions/api/fetch_team_table.py and web/pages/api/Teams/nst-team-stats.ts form the current Python proxy boundary. The web proxy sends planned-request/admission-budget headers and has its own persistence/processing after the HTTP exchange; a backend per-request finish cannot stand in for parent whole-job completion. Both source files and their listed tests remain retained/idle.

Seven other direct-client consumers outside the already-transferred goalie route are listed with exact recorded custody. An empty owner list means no matching exact claim observed in the two inspected registries, not a custody grant or proof nobody edits it. Existing imports do not establish whole-job lease participation.

No legacy Python/proxy/other direct caller source is transferred by this receipt. Coordinate only the concrete enclosing hooks needed after the lifecycle design is reviewable. New service/SQL paths need exact allocation in the recipient lane; do not edit or replace the immutable accepted SQL artifact.

lifecycleContractEvidence.existingSharedAdmission: nst_admit_attempt_v1 has global rolling attempt timestamps and spacing, with a 1000ms dispatch TTL. It has no job owner/token, start/end receipt, heartbeat or whole-job occupancy state. No admission timestamp, elapsed gap, missing audit, or cleared rate window proves a direct job ended.
lifecycleContractEvidence.localBudget: requestBudget.ts active/urlHash records cover one local request attempt and are conservative on an unfinished attempt. They are same-user filesystem coordination, explicitly not a cross-host job lease or global completion receipt.
lifecycleContractEvidence.audit: withCronJobAudit wraps web handlers and persists a final audit outcome. It has no NST lease. Its finally path is not guaranteed after process death and cannot establish Python/proxy job finality. Preserve business outcome versus audit durability and retrySafe:false holds.
lifecycleContractEvidence.newGoalieCheckpoint: Successor-owned 20261101161622_nst_goalie_catchup_v1.sql has cohort claim/finish/hold receipts, a disabled control row, and a direct-finish/clearance requirement. Its comment says no automatic producer establishes those attestations. It is not an implemented shared direct-job occupancy service. An expired or unacknowledged claim remains unknown/review-required, never proof of completed output.
lifecycleContractEvidence.smallestBoundary: An NST-specific lifecycle at the enclosing job/orchestrator boundary, with explicit shared owner/token and start/finish evidence covering request fan-out and durable output/checkpoint finalization, is the focused integration boundary. Do not open and close a whole-job lease per client fetch, infer it from audit presence, or make expiry imply success. Transport adapters alone cannot attest the enclosing multi-request job ended.
lifecycleContractEvidence.implementationStatus: Boundary guidance only. This custodian has implemented no lifecycle service and has not validated the successor-reported108 offline tests / 11 local PostgreSQL scenario groups. Existing checkpoint remains disabled; no enabled/production health claim.
